events.title: Duar War and the Treaty of Sinchula
hints: A diplomatic insult to an envoy led to a short war in the mountains.
Fertile foothill passes called duars were lost.
A treaty signed in 1865 swapped territory for an annual allowance.
events.summary: After a British mission was mistreated in 1864, Britain went to war and Bhutan lost the Bengal Duars and other territory in the Treaty of Sinchula (1865), roughly a fifth of its land. In return it received an annual payment, and the Duars later became a tea-growing region.
events.quip: A fifth of the country traded for an annual allowance: history's least generous subscription plan.

events.title: Treaty of Punakha
hints: A king agreed to be guided by a distant empire in foreign policy.
It was signed at a mountain fortress in January 1910.
A larger annual subsidy was part of the bargain.
events.summary: In the 1910 Treaty of Punakha, Bhutan accepted British guidance in its external relations in exchange for a larger subsidy and a promise of non-interference in its internal affairs. The arrangement made the Himalayan kingdom a buffer between British India and Tibet.
